sp_paragraph: GJ 685 (1 -> 3): GJ 684 A and B (26 Dra A, B) added; GJ 685 stays the host row as the planet host. Physical association: MSC 'Cmpr'; Sperauskas et al. 2019 (A&A 626, A31) find C's RV constant and equal to A's; parallaxes 69.89 (C) and 69.28 mas (AB, unresolved); Cifuentes et al. 2025 list the pair. Masses 1.07 and 0.70 M-sun are the MSC's estimates (Soederhjelm's dynamical sum 1.72 M-sun agrees); classes G0 V (MSC) and K3 V (Edwards 1976); A's Teff 5925 K (Luck 2017). Orbit: ORB6 / Soederhjelm 1999 (P 76.1 yr, a 1.53 arcsec, e 0.18). INFERRED (orange): the A-B semi-major axis, 21.5 AU = 1.53 arcsec / 71.0 mas (Soederhjelm's own parallax); Kepler check 1.73 M-sun against his 1.72; +/- 1% from his parallax error, 3% if Gaia's is used instead. INFERRED (orange): GJ 684 A's separation from GJ 685, 10561.5 AU = rho 738.16 arcsec (Gaia DR3 positions; the AB photocentre) x GJ 685's Gaia DR3 distance (69.8921 mas); identical to Cifuentes et al. 2025's published 10561.5 au; a sky-plane lower bound.
flags: GJ 684 AB's Gaia DR3 proper motion differs from GJ 685's by ~56 mas/yr (3.8 km/s), far above the escape speed at 10,600 AU. That is A's 76 yr orbital motion in the unresolved photocentre (A's reflex speed ~3-4 km/s near the 2023 periastron), and it is why the Gaia co-moving pass missed the pair. RV (C constant and equal to A: Sperauskas et al. 2019) and parallax support a physical system.

Masses of GJ 684 A and B are the MSC's photometric estimates, not dynamical; the only dynamical value is the 1.72 M-sun sum. No resolved luminosity exists for either star, so both rows will show 'no luminosity on file'.
The Known tab lists 'GJ 684 AB' (Gaia DR3 1439121018358632832) as a separate unplotted system; it is now part of GJ 685's.
The host GJ 685 is not the system's most massive star (as with WD 1856+534); companions are placed relative to it.

sp_paragraph: Gl 49 (1 -> 2): GJ 51 B (Wolf 47 = V388 Cas) added. Class, Teff, L, R and mass as published in Cifuentes et al. 2020 (A&A 642, A115; VOSA SED fits); RV Fouque et al. 2018 (MNRAS 475, 1960); PM Gaia DR3 522864272041351296. Three precise RVs of B since 2018 (CARMENES, the SPIRou input catalogue, a 2022 survey) agree with A's to 0.5 km/s, and Cifuentes et al. 2025's multiplicity census lists no spectroscopic companion. The typical-companion rule (0.07 M-sun at 0.3 AU) would give K ~ 7 km/s over a ~107 d period, which those RVs would very likely have shown.

This is weaker than GJ 896's refutation -- no paper says 'activity' or 'single' in words -- but all precise RVs of B (-6.29 CARMENES / Reiners 2018, -5.76 +/- 0.02 Fouque 2018, -5.88 +/- 0.50 in 2022ApJ...935..104) match A within 0.5 km/s, the one discrepant RV (+6.7 km/s, West et al. 2015) is an outlier, and Cifuentes et al. 2025 do not flag B as an SB. If the owner wants the hollow row anyway: 'GJ 51 Bb', counted, Separation blank (the 0.3 AU typical rule is excluded by those RVs: K ~ 7 km/s), Stars = 3.

The MSC's suspected Aa,Ab ('a?', comment 'RUWE=7.2') is not counted: A's Gaia astrometric excess is what its known planets produce -- McArthur et al. 2010 (ApJ 715, 1203) measured c's and d's astrometric orbits with HST, and d alone moves the star ~1.4 mas on a 3.5 yr period, longer than Gaia DR3's 34 months -- and A is a G = 4.0 star, where Gaia DR3 astrometry is poorly calibrated. sp_paragraph: ups And (1 -> 2): ups And B added. Class M4.5 V (Lowrance et al. 2002, ApJ 572, L79); mass 0.171 M-sun and Teff 3195 K (Mugrauer 2019, MNRAS 490, 5088); RV and PM Gaia DR3 348020242217448576. No luminosity published, left blank. NOT ADDED: the MSC's suspected Aa,Ab ('a?', RUWE 7.2). It is explained without a companion: planet d's reflex orbit is ~1.4 mas (a 2.53 AU, ~10 M-Jup dynamical mass: McArthur et al. 2010, Deitrick et al. 2015) with P = 3.5 yr, unmodelled by Gaia DR3's single-star fit, plus the bright-star (G = 4) calibration; the typical companion (0.38 M-sun at 3 AU) would drive K ~ 5 km/s, excluded by 14 yr of m/s RVs.
flags: AUDIT TARGET WAS 3, PROPOSED 2: the MSC's suspected Aa,Ab ('a?', 'RUWE=7.2') is not counted. It rests only on A's Gaia DR3 RUWE, which the known planets explain (d's ~1.4 mas astrometric orbit, measured with HST by McArthur et al. 2010) together with G = 4 bright-star calibration; a stellar companion is excluded by 974 RVs over 14 yr (McArthur et al. 2010). Like gam Cep Ab / tau Boo Ab, this is the planets, not a star. If the owner keeps the '?' rule anyway, the row would have a blank separation: the 3 AU typical rule is excluded by the RVs.

sp_paragraph: VHS J125601.92-125723.9 (1 -> 2): the host's binary companion B added. All values published in Dupuy et al. 2023, MNRAS 519, 1688: orbit (a 1.96 AU, P 7.31 yr, e 0.883), total mass 0.141 M-sun with 74 M-Jup = 0.0706 M-sun per component for a near-unity mass ratio, component luminosities log L = -2.982 (A) and -2.994 (B) at the Gaia EDR3 distance, cooling age 140 +/- 20 Myr; class M7.5 (Gauza et al. 2015, unresolved). The host row's luminosity is overridden with Dupuy's A value: the Systems tab's 0.0007244 is consistent with the pair's combined light at the superseded 78.8 mas parallax. No orange cells: the masses and luminosities are unit conversions of published values. The new star is named B (Dupuy et al.), not the MSC's Ab; the MSC's B is the planet-mass b.
flags: SYSTEMS TAB LUMINOSITY LOOKS STALE: Host luminosity 0.0007244 L-sun (log -3.14) matches the A+B combined light scaled to Gauza et al. 2015's 78.8 mas parallax ((12.69 / 21.14 pc)^2 x 10^-2.687 = 7.4e-4) -- an inference; the cell names no source. Dupuy et al. 2023 give log L = -2.982 per component at the Gaia distance (0.00104). The Multi-stars host row is overridden here; the Systems cell, its solvent bands and the Planets tab's host luminosity for b still use the old value and are for the owner to decide.

Naming: the new star is 'VHS J125601.92-125723.9 B' (Dupuy et al. 2023's A / B / b). The MSC's 'VHS 1256 B' is the planet b, and catalog_loader.match_key() folds 'X B' and 'X b' together -- the same pattern as 41 existing Multi-stars rows (tau Boo B / tau Boo b, 55 Cnc B, ...). If the owner prefers no case-only collision here, use the MSC's 'Ab' instead.

The per-component mass (0.0706 M-sun) assumes Dupuy's near-unity mass ratio; their direct fit is poorly constrained (M_A/M_tot = 0.45 +/- 0.08). The host's Systems mass 0.07 is consistent and left alone.
The planet b (16.0 M-Jup on Planets, '>13 MJ - likely BD') stays a planet under the owner's rule for brown dwarfs already on Planets (Dupuy et al. 2023: 12.0 or 16 M-Jup, bimodal).
